You can automate a task you do every week without writing a single line of code.

21,000 people just saved one engineer's guide to doing it. Almost everyone gets step 1 wrong: they give AI a to-do list when it needed a goal.

"Send the invoice" is a step. "Get paid within 7 days" is the goal. Hand AI the goal and it can find a faster process than yours.

5 prompts. Run them in order in Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini, then put the last one on a schedule.

Prompt 1: Goal first
"I want to hand you a task I do every [day/week]. Don't help with steps yet. Ask me what this task is really for: does it make money, save money or save time, and how will I know it worked? Then write the goal back in one sentence I can measure."

Prompt 2: Brain dump
"Here's how I do it today, unsorted: [paste or dictate everything: steps, apps, where the information comes from, how I check it's right, what usually goes wrong]. Don't fix anything yet. Restate my process as numbered steps and mark every step where you'd need access to something."

Prompt 3: Find what I forgot
"Ask me one question at a time about what I do without thinking: which source wins when two disagree, when you should stop and ask me, what done looks like. After 5 questions, walk me through 3 real examples and how you'd handle each."

Prompt 4: Beat my process
"Compare my process to the goal. Which step can you cut, merge or speed up? What would you do differently if this task was yours? Give me the new version and what could break."

Prompt 5: Autopilot
"Turn this into one set of instructions you can run on a schedule every [Monday 9am]. Include what to check first, what to send me, and when to stop and wait for my OK."

Run prompt 1 on the task you hate most. In 10 minutes you'll know if it's worth automating.

We've had hundreds of calls with execs (F500s, T20 PE Firms, etc), and I fed notes from the last 25 into Claude to answer the question: "What are companies struggling with, when it comes to AI Transformation?"

It gave a really good response:

[We fix all 10 of these at Varick. Work with us below.]

1. They're improving one step but not seeing end-to-end impact. The amount of hands-on cycle time in most processes is 1-5%, and that's the part that gets faster while people outside the process wait. The engineering org that writes twice as much code but isn't shipping faster. The equipment dealer that's had a vendor come in and work for months to automate one step of an 8 step order processing process. Most point solutions are 1/20th of the value people think they are.

2. They're treating workflows as if they're exceptions. >25% of invoices come in without a PO for this finance team, and as the head of the process said, "statistically they won't be exceptions. They will be the norm." Which is why anyone who's seen a process end-to-end immediately discounts demos people bring in, which are almost always the happy path only.

3. They're catching errors based on size, not based on good controls. I spoke with an Accounts Receivable team that bills a partner based on tickets with free text fields that, to put it politely, have been incorrect or required rework in 5 of the last 8 quarters. Why didn't they catch it? Well if the team credits the partner for $3M they'll catch it at close, but if they credit the partner for $20k they won't. As one person on the team said, "Humans. Humans catch it."

4. IT owns AI and part of their job is to say no. Spoke with a bank, a software company, and an insurance company in one day who said they've been blocked on everything by IT. One engineer told me he spent a month and $600 of his own money building a multi-agent system in Claude to help with a design process. And while he can spend $600 personally, he's only allowed to spend $150/mo on AI at work, and the company won't even let him buy a subscription.

5. They don't have accessible data. Sales can't connect to Salesforce until they "clean up the data." Their ERP doesn't have OAuth so they can only log in with a username and password. One engineering team's design data is a 648GB zip file that drops every 5-10 hours. Most prototypes get to demos because they're built on static data, and then can't move to production because real processes need real-time data.

6. They don't have good process docs, and even if they did they wouldn't be accurate. As one person told me, the SOPs for their processes are "on random SharePoints everywhere. A treasure hunt." Plus, when we mine the systems of record our process maps generally have ~20% more steps than what companies think is in the process.

7. Legal needs tracking, not contract drafting. I spoke with a legal team that had ~8,000 tickets last year, the vast majority administrative. Another legal team said they generally track contracts until the first draft is complete, and then the system no longer tracks them. As they told me, "the default is, it's legal. It's always our fault." And none of these teams can track how long things take, which is a problem when they need to ask for more headcount and the answer they get is, "okay prove it."

8. The last consulting engagement they had only provided numbers, not a path forward. In the words of one person I spoke with: "they gave us a lot of numbers. But the how is really the most complex thing." Even engineering teams are being asked by boards what they're measuring, and most can only provide metrics around merge requests.

9. Most companies don't have agent sprawl but they do have agent nothing. People are building agents for themselves but they're the spreadsheets of 2026: only the people that built them know how they work, and they'll keep running after those people move on. Meanwhile the companies that we're talking to that are backed by PEs and have real moats in their businesses told us that agent sprawl "would be a good problem if we had it."

10. They're betting on the team, not on the method. In the words of one person I spoke with, "everybody has a story. Pitch went great and then project went terrible. And the difference is the person that walked in the door."

Nick Bostrom says delaying superintelligence carries risks of its own. Every year of delay could postpone medical breakthroughs that extend human life and reduce suffering.

Furthermore, AI's upside could extend far beyond longer lives and higher living standards, opening up new possibilities for human intelligence, emotional depth, creativity, and connection.

Nick joins a16z's Eddy Lazzarin and Elena Burger to discuss what people misunderstand about his views, what “deep utopia” means, and what human purpose might look like in a world with superintelligence.

"Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares had this book, 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.' And it seemed to me that we have at least as strong evidence for the claim that if nobody builds it, everyone dies."

"Successfully developing safe superintelligence, I think could lead to enormous breakthroughs in biomedicine and in anti-aging interventions that could radically extend the lifespan of currently existing people."

"If you think about what our life expectancy would be if we weren't aging, it's something on the order of 1,200, maybe 1,400 years or so. And that maybe is a quite conservative lower bound because in this situation you might also have other ways of reducing other mortality risks like accidents and so forth."

"You might think that if we spend more time doing AI alignment research, the existential risk from developing AI goes down at some rate. And then on the other hand, every year that we delay it, we have millions and millions of people dying."

"You don't want to delay a single day longer than you really need to."

quoted_tweet.author: Fireside Alpha
quoted_tweet.text:
Dario Amodei says Anthropic could drive at 200 miles an hour but chooses 90

“So this is one of the central tensions at the heart of the company, but it’s really because this technology is so powerful, it has so many effects in the world. It’s something that every company in this space will have to face, whether they want to or not. We’re just facing it more explicitly and more thoughtfully. And so you think about something like pacing.”

“The idea behind pacing was, imagine that you’re driving your car at 60 miles an hour, and then you discover or invent something that could let you drive the car at 200 miles an hour. This is models building themselves, recursive self-improvement. What we’ve done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let’s only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus, we spend building the model in the right way.”

“And I think in the long run, that will work out pretty well for the investors as well, because the company that builds the safest, that has the trust of the customers and the enterprises of the world, I think that is the company that’s going to be both best for society and, in the long run, I hope, best for the performance of the company.”

text:
卧槽，大肥鱼 DeepSeek harness这次又经验全场了！

OpenMotion 可能是我最近看到最猛的开源 AI 视频项目之一

它基本可以看作是剪映 + Claude Motion 的开源替代

而且不是那种只能看看 Demo 的半成品，是已经能真正拿来做视频工作流的工具

最关键的是，它直接把最近 Opus 5.5、Fable 5.2 这套 Motion 动效视频的最佳实践都给浓缩进去了

甚至连 DeepSeek 这波动态设计升级，也有人已经用 OpenMotion 跑出来了

像 Gemini Tasks、dots、Claude Duet、Grok Bot、Muse 这种风格的视频，现在都能拿它来复刻、拆解、重做

最狠的是，它还支持 22 种 Agent
Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、OpenCode 这些都能接

也就是说，以后做产品宣传视频、功能演示视频、动态设计视频，可能真的不用再纯手搓剪辑了
你给它一个参考视频
它就能帮你分析镜头、字幕、转场、动效结构
然后生成一个可编辑版本
后面继续改文案、换画面、调时间轴，全部都能接着做

支持导出 MP4、MOV、WebM、GIF
这就不是“能不能玩”的问题了，而是谁先拿它卷内容产能

开源地址
https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/integrations/dsh/README.md

quoted_tweet.text:
卧槽！做网站、做前端、用 Codex 的有福了！之前需要收费的现在免费了！动画设计师要失业了

以前需要 Club GSAP 会员才能使用的 SplitText、MorphSVG 等插件，现在全部免费开放，连商业项目也能使用，不需要会员、不需要私有 npm 仓库或额外授权 Token

而且官方还开源了一套 GSAP AI Skills，支持 Codex、Claude Code、Cursor、Windsurf 等 40 多种 AI 编程工具

GitHub 已经拿下 18.7K Stars，这次是真的值得收藏！

前端他都能干：

1、自动生成高级网页动画

让 AI 帮你制作丝滑的页面转场、元素入场、文字动画、交互效果，不用每次从零研究动画 API

2、滚动视差动画

ScrollTrigger 专项 Skill，可以实现滚动触发、页面固定、视差效果、滚动进度联动动画

3、复杂时间轴动画

多个元素依次出现、交错运动、连续转场，都能让 AI 按照正确的时间轴逻辑编写

4、文字和 SVG 动画

支持 SplitText、MorphSVG 等插件的使用指导，制作文字拆分、字符逐个出现、SVG 形状变换

5、React / Vue / Svelte 支持

针对不同前端框架提供专门指导，处理动画生命周期、组件清理等问题

6、动画性能优化

优化动画属性、减少不必要的布局计算，让网页动起来更丝滑

最重要的是：官方提供了 8 个专业 AI Skills

涵盖 GSAP 核心动画、时间轴、滚动动画、插件、工具函数、React、性能优化和其他前端框架

安装不需要自己敲命令，直接把下面这段提示词发给 Codex 或 Claude Code：

“请帮我安装 GSAP 官方 AI Skills

GitHub 仓库地址：
https://github.com/greensock/gsap-skills

请使用当前 AI 编程工具支持的 Skills 安装方式，自动识别当前工具，并安装仓库中的全部 8 个 Skills 到正确目录。

安装完成后，请检查是否安装成功，列出已安装的 Skills，并确保后续开发网页动画时能够自动调用这些技能。

如果需要执行终端命令或授权，请提示我完成相应操作。”

以前需要自己研究半天的复杂网页动效，现在可以让 AI 参考官方的专业开发规范来完成了
